about.title: El Centro Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a family member in a traffic collision changes everything, and it often happens without warning on roads El Centro residents drive every day, like Main, La Brucherie, or Imperial. Public records show El Centro saw 2 traffic deaths and dozens of injury collisions in the most recent reporting year, a reminder that these losses touch real families in this community. California law allows certain surviving family members, usually a spouse, domestic partner, or children first, to pursue a wrongful death claim against the party responsible. These cases are separate from any criminal proceedings and follow their own civil process and deadlines. Our team reviews what happened, explains your standing under California law, and helps you understand next steps. We work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless your family recovers compensation.

items.title: Understanding Who Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to specific people, typically a spouse, domestic partner, or children first, then other dependents or heirs. We can help clarify where your family stands.

items.title: Awareness of Strict Deadlines
items.desc: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim, though claims against a government entity carry a much shorter window. Missing these deadlines can end a claim before it starts.

items.title: No Upfront Cost to Your Family
items.desc: We work on contingency, so there's no fee unless there's a recovery. That means families in El Centro can seek guidance without added financial pressure during an already difficult time.

items.question: Who is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: California law generally gives priority to a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children to bring the claim. If none of those exist, certain other dependents or heirs may have standing. We can review your specific family situation to explain who qualifies.

items.question: How long do we have to file after losing a family member in El Centro?
items.answer: In most cases, California allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim. That window is often much shorter if a government entity, such as a public road authority, may be involved. It's worth speaking with us promptly so deadlines aren't missed.

items.question: What kinds of compensation can a wrongful death claim cover?
items.answer: Recoverable losses can include funeral and burial costs, the financial support the deceased would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. Every case is different, and we can walk through what may apply given your circumstances.
